data.name: Calixus
data.gender_notes: Calixus is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Calixus is a Latin name derived from the word 'calix', meaning 'cup' or 'chalice'. In Christian tradition, this name can refer to the chalice used in the Eucharist during Mass. The name Calixus carries the meaning “Little cup, chalice” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Latin. Parents who choose Calixus usually hope their child will grow to embody little cup, chalice and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Calixus is a name deeply rooted in Christian symbolism, representing the cup or chalice used during the sacrament of the Eucharist. This name embodies the deep faith and devotion to God that is central to Christian beliefs.
data.etymology: Calixus belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Little cup, chalice.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Calixus total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

data.cultural_impact: In the Middle Ages, Calixus was a popular name for Christian monks and saints as a reminder of the cup used in the celebration of the Holy Eucharist, emphasizing their dedication to the religious order and devotion to God.
data.spiritual_significance: Calixus represents the cup of God's Love, offering and receiving the unchanging presence of Christ in our daily lives. The name embodies a deep connection to the spiritual beliefs of the Christian faith, emphasizing reverence and devotion to God.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Calixus: Vessel of the Chalice. Symbolizing the deep connection between the believer and the divine, as they share in the Eucharistic feast.

biblical_reference.note: not directly mentioned in the Bible, but related to Eucharistic symbolism

historical_references.reference: Calixus I was a pope who ruled from AD 432 to 442. He is best known for his efforts to strengthen the power of the papacy and his role in the Councils of Ephesus and Chalcedon. At the Council of Ephesus, he confirmed the deposition of Nestorius and upheld the title 'Mother of God' for Mary.

Calixus III, born in Naples in 1430, was Pope from 1455 to 1458. He is known for his efforts to reform the papacy and the Church, including the suppression of simony and the promotion of the study of Greek and Hebrew.

Overall, the use of the name 'Calixus' in these contexts reflects a trend towards immersive, interactive experiences and a revived interest in historical and mythological themes.
